source_notes: The Open University's detailed module handbooks, unit materials and current-year assessment guides are gated behind its student VLE and were not accessible; the QAA Subject Benchmark Statement for Law (2023, openly published) is used as the umbrella threshold academic standard for every stage's rubric instead of inventing OU-specific numeric mark bands.

A small number of genuinely open, third-party-rehosted OU module descriptions and past-student materials (not the current year, which is VLE-gated) were traceable for some subjects — Contract Law, Criminal Law, Tort Law, Family Law, Property Law, Commercial Law, Jurisprudence and Legal Theory, and Equity and Trusts — and were used to sharpen that stage's pass_threshold language; Legal System and Method, Public Law, Alternative Dispute Resolution and Dissertation could not be backward-resolved to an open module-specific report, and rest on the QAA benchmark alone, stated honestly rather than papered over.

Doctrinal content (case law, statutes, the shape of each topic) is itemised from standard, universally-taught qualifying-law-degree topic lists, not from the OU's own gated unit-by-unit numbering, and every case and statute cited is real, checkable, well-known English authority.
